title: Viniyoga of āyātu

words.role: first word of the anuvāka quoted

words.meaning: thus; marks the words before it as a quotation
of the anuvāka (the section of recitation)

words.role: with the seer’s name: ‘the seer is …’

words.meaning: anuṣṭubh, the metre of four lines of eight syllables

sandhi.rule: u before a vowel becomes v; i before a vowel becomes y
-aḥ before a vowel other than a loses its visarga

translation.literal: Of the anuvāka “āyātu”: Vāmadeva the seer; anuṣṭubh the metre; Gāyatrī the deity.
translation.readable: Āyātu varadā devī: seer Vāmadeva, metre anuṣṭubh, deity the Gāyatrī.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: āyātu varadā devī (Mahānārāyaṇa 10.34), the verse that invites the Gāyatrī before the japa. S stops at the deity; M adds the use, āvāhane viniyogaḥ, ‘used in the invocation’ (corrections.json).
in_the_rite: Step avahana, before āyātu varadā devī, in all three services.
